classification.difficultyReason: The hardest demand combines the right-angle marker with the supplied tiger and lion angles to find the remaining sector. Finding the lion count then applies its angular share to 20 animals; these are short, routine linked applications of the taught whole-circle relationships.

content.prompt: The sector graph represents 20 big cats in a zoo.

spec.description: Unfilled four-sector circle with singular lowercase labels and a right-angle square in the upper-left cheetah sector. Ordinary outlines and labels are black.
spec.mathematics: Clockwise from the upward radius: tiger 144°, lion 54°, jaguar 72°, cheetah 90°. Only the cheetah right-angle marker appears in the diagram; the numerical tiger and lion angles remain in part b.
spec.answerVisibility: Category labels, boundaries and the right-angle square are givens. No numerical answers appear in the diagram.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What percentage of animals are cheetahs?

answer.worked:
The right-angle marker gives a sector angle of $90^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Cheetah percentage}&=\frac{90}{360}\times100\%\\&=25\%\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the tigers are represented by a sector with angle $144^\circ$ and the lions represented by a sector with angle $54^\circ$, what is the angle of the sector representing jaguars?

children.label: c
children.prompt: How many lions are in the zoo?
